statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail risk is 20%, the floor of the watch band, after the Nasdaq-100 closed at 30,501.56 having fully retraced its morning low, while Stress stays high at 74% with the 30-year near a 24-year peak and Brent above $100.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the mapped state is WATCH for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The narrow evidence-based danger window spans the 12:30Z September employment report through the hour after the 13:30Z US cash open on 2 October, which contains the single forecast hour mapped to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this assessment.
headline: Nasdaq-100 closes a fully retraced session as yields retreat from a 24-year peak, with the September employment report the next scheduled checkpoint
body:
Verified evidence at the assessment cutoff covers a completed US cash session and the first minutes after the futures reopen. The Nasdaq-100 closed at 30,501.56, up 93.06 points or 0.31% from a 30,408.50 previous close, inside a 30,274.65-30,616.24 range and 269 points below the 30,770.63 52-week high. The structural fact that matters most for this strategy is the shape of that path: the index opened higher, sank to its session low as long-dated yields climbed, then recovered through the afternoon as yields eased. A session low that is fully retraced before the close is two-way price discovery, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure that defines Tail risk, so Tail stays at the 20% floor of the watch band.

Cross-asset evidence is genuinely mixed rather than aligned. The 10-year Treasury yield closed at 5.24%, down about six basis points, after touching 5.34% intraday, its highest since 2002; the 2-year fell 10.6 basis points to 4.80% and the 5-year sits at 5.01%, while the 30-year near 5.62% remains close to a 24-year high following the worst bond quarter in decades. Implied volatility decayed rather than expanded, with the VIX closing at 16.39 after a 17.59 session high. Against that, WTI settled at 92.91 dollars, up 2.75%, and Brent moved above 100 dollars, up roughly 4.3%, after Chinese refiners suspended exports of refined products beyond Hong Kong and Macau. September ISM manufacturing held in expansion at 54.5, but its prices paid index jumped 6.8 points to 77.9, the highest since May and a 24th consecutive month of rising input costs. Energy and input-cost pressure of that kind is an inflation channel into the long end; it elevates Stress and keeps the yield backdrop heavy without, on its own, implying a pathological equity price path.

Sector evidence was supportive rather than fragile. Micron's results and its guidance of about 61.5 billion dollars of first-quarter revenue against roughly 57 billion expected carried semiconductors, and the same tone lifted the Nikkei 2.8% to 68,606.81. Labour data released on 1 October was firm, with initial claims at 197,000 and continuing claims at 1,701,000.

The next scheduled checkpoint is the September employment report at 12:30Z on 2 October. Published previews point to roughly 90,000 to 95,000 payrolls after August's 162,000, with unemployment seen unchanged at 4.1% and average hourly earnings at 0.3% month over month. That release has not printed at the assessment cutoff, so no post-event structure is treated as observed. Under this repository's risk contract, event importance and wide estimate dispersion raise Stress and reduce Confidence rather than Tail; Tail rises only when a path is actually observed to deny retracement. The forecast therefore carries a single orange hour at the 13:30Z cash open, where an opening auction extending a fresh post-release move with shallow pullbacks is the specific structure that would overwhelm mean reversion.

Evidence limitations are stated plainly. NQ futures reopened at 21:00Z from the 20:00Z-21:00Z daily halt, and the available futures quote is delayed and timestamped before the halt, so it is not live post-reopen price-path evidence. The shared Finviz context file was collected on 29 September and reports partial status, so it is stale under the 90-minute freshness rule and was not used; all evidence above comes from independent current research. Confidence is 88% on verified index, volatility, yield, energy, macro-release and catalyst levels, reduced from higher only by the absent live futures path.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hours are available from published Claude assessments. Tail ranged 20-25% and the mapped state was WATCH in 23 of the 24 hours, with a single orange BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES hour at 06:00Z when Tail touched 25% during a trend-up European phase. Stress climbed from 70-71% overnight to a 78% peak across 14:00-15:00Z as the global bond selloff pushed the 10-year to a 24-year high, then eased to 74-76% as yields retreated into the cash close. Confidence held 87-89% throughout.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds the watch band through the post-close futures hours, the Asian session and the European morning, with Tail at 20-22% and dominant mode normal to mixed while China's National Day holiday thins regional flow. Risk then builds into 2 October: Tail reaches 23% in the pre-release hour, 24% for the 12:30Z September employment report and 25% at the 13:30Z cash open, the single orange hour inside the narrow 12:30Z-14:30Z danger window, before easing to 20-22% as post-event price discovery is scored. Stress peaks at 79% across the release and the open, then decays to 74% by the 20:00Z close and futures halt. Confidence drifts from 88% to 84-85% as the verified US reference ages and the unprinted release widens the outcome range.
